properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 967073 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: HALLIBURTON
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 967073
Incident Time: 2011-02-10 12:00:00
Nearest City: Bonanza Utah, UT
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: BC-200 UC
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: HALLIBURTON
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 325 gallons
EMPLOYEES WERE PREPARING CHEMICALS TO PUMP ON A STIMULATION JOB ON AN OIL AN GAS LOCATION. EMPLOYEES PREPARED A TOTE OF BC-200 UC FOR TRANSFER THROUGH A HOSE AND THEN REALIZED IS WAS TOO COLD TO PUMP THAT PARTICULAR TOTE. FLUID WAS COLD ENOUGH IT WAS NOT MOVING. EMPLOYEES THEN MOVED HOSES TO ANOTHER TOTE AND PUMPED THAT TOTE. EMPLOYEES FINISHED FOR THE DAY AND THEN BLANKETED THE CHEMICALS AND PUT A HEATER UNDER THE BLANKETS TO HELP KEEP THE CHEMICALS WARM. EMPLOYEES THEN LEFT THE LOCATION FOR THE NIGHT. WHEN EMPLOYEES ARRIVED BACK ON LOCATION THEY DISCOVERED A SPILL OF 325 GALLONS OF BC-200 UC. IT IS BELIEVED THAT THEY FAILED TO COMPLETELY CLOSE THE VALVE ON THE CHEMICAL TOTE WHEN THEY TRANSFERRED HOSES AND AS THE HEATER WARMED THE CHEMICAL UP IT ALLOWED IT TO BEGIN MOVING AND RELEASED THE CONTENTS OF THE TOTE ONTO THE GROUND.

properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 885792 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: TEDIA COMPANY
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 885792
Incident Time: 2008-09-14 09:00:00
Nearest City: Fairfield, OH
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: 1,4-DIOXANE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: TEDIA COMPANY
Skytruth Analysis
WHILE DISTILLING 1,4-DIOXANE, ON OR ABOUT 10:00AM 9/13/08, THE CONDENSER FROZE UP FORCING VAPOR BACK THROUGH THE STILL INTO THE PRODUCTION FACILITY. THE REACTOR ROOM FILLED WITH VAPOR WHICH ESCAPED THE FACILITY THROUGH NATURAL VENTILATION. ABOUT 0400 9/14/08, THE RELEASE WAS DISCOVERED. THE STILL WAS SHUTDOWN AND REMAINING VAPOR WAS VENTED OUTSIDE THE FACILITY BY A CEILING FAN. ABOUT 3564 LBS OF MATERIAL WAS LOST FROM THE STILL AND ASSUMED TO BE RELEASED INTO THE ATMOSPHERE AS VAPOR. WIND STORMS CAUSED POWER OUTAGE ABOUT MIDDAY 9/14/08 LASTING UNTIL 9/18/08, WHEN RELEASE WAS REPORTED TO COMPANY MANGERS. ERRONEOUS ASSUMPTIONS OF HOW MUCH VAPOR WAS RELEASED INTO THE ATMOSPHERE WERE MADE INITIALLY, BUT CALCULATIONS PERFORMED ON 9/29/08 INDICATED NEARLY ALL OF MATERIAL WAS RELEASED OUTSIDE THE FACILITY.

properties.title: NRC Report: Jet Fuel: Jp-8 in Unknown near Hickam Airforce Base, HI
properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 800671 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: 15 LRS FUELS LOGISTICS
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 800671
Incident Time: 2006-06-13 23:15:00
Nearest City: Hickam Airforce Base, HI
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: JET FUEL: JP-8
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: 15 LRS FUELS LOGISTICS
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
///WEB REPORT/// A JP-8 FUEL WAS DISCOVERED AS THE FUEL WAS TRANSFERRED TO A 500 GALLON CAPACITY, JP-8 RECLAIM AST#3, WHICH IS PART OF A PRESSURIZED SYSTEM. THE RELIEF VALVE FAILED, CAUSING AN OVERFLOW. THE PRODUCT DIRECTLY SOUTH TOWARD THE AIRCRAFT RAMP. AN AREA OF SOIL APPROXIMATELY 40 FT LONG BY 15 FT WIDE WAS IMPACTED. ABSORBENTS WERE IMMEDIATELY USED. THE SPILL THEN FLOWED WEST ALONG THE ACCESS ROAD AND EDGE OF THE RAMP, WHERE THERE IS A STORM WATER DRAIN INLET. THE DRAIN AND THE NEXT DRAIN DOWN GRADIENT HAD VERY LITTLE WATER AND A SHEEN. 15 LRS FUELS VACUUMED BOTH SW INLETS OUT,COLLECTING APPROX. 15 GALLONS OF WATER/FUEL MIXTURE. THE SW DRAIN EXTENDS UNDER THE RAMP/TAXIWAY AND ENTERS KUMUMAUU CANAL NEAR AREA 6. A BOOM IS IN PLACE DIRECTLY ADJACENT TOTHE OUTFALL OF THESE SW INLETS TO THE CANAL; AND TWO OTHER BOOMS ARE IN PLACE FURTHER DOWNSTREAM OF THE CANAL NEAR MAMALA BAY DRIVE. DOWNSTREAM SW DRAIN INLETS AND THE AREA NEAR THE OUTFALL WERE CHECKED BY BASE FIRE DEPT. AND DID NOT HAVE ANY OBSERVABLE SHEEN OR ODOR. THE SETIMATED TOTAL RELEASE IS ESTIMATED AT LESS THAN 100 GALLONS. 15 CES ENVIRONMENTAL FLIGHT WAS CONTACTED BY BASE FIRE DEPT. ON 14/06/06 @ 0700, AND THE INVESTIGATION WAS COMPLETED ON 14/06/06 @ 0830.

Suspected Responsible Party: STOLTHAVEN HOUSTON INC.
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 29.772108, -95.176929 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 1680 gallon
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** APPROXIMATELY 40-BARRELS OF 1-OCTENE (C-8 NORMAL ALPHA OLEFIN) WERE RELEASED INTO THE MANIFOLD DRIP PAN OF A BARGE DOCKED AT STOLTHAVEN HOUSTON'S BARGE DOCK-C. THE BARGE WAS BEING PREPARED TO LOAD 1-OCTENE FROM A SHORE TANK AT THE STOLTHAVEN HOUSTON TERMINAL WHEN THE PRODUCT WAS INADVERTENTLY RELEASED FROM THE END OF THE MARINE TRANSFER HOSE INTO THE BARGE'S DRIP PAN PRIOR TO COMMENCING THIS PLANNED TRANSFER OPERATION. THE DRIP PAN FILLED WITH 1-OCTENE PRODUCT, SUBSEQUENTLY CAUSING AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT TO SPILL FROM THE CONTAINED DRIP PAN AREA INTO THE HOUSTON SHIP CHANNEL. NOTE THAT THE RELEASE QUANTITY PROVIDED IS AN INITIAL ESTIMATE ONLY. A MORE DETAILED CALCULATION WILL BE PERFORMED BASED ON STORAGE TANK INVENTORIES. NOTE THAT 1-OCTENE DOES NOT HAVE A LISTED REPORTABLE QUANTITY (RQ) IN 40 CFR SECTION §302.4. THE RELEASE HAS BEEN STOPPED AND THE NECESSARY CLEAN-UP EFFORTS HAVE BEEN COMPLETED. THERE WAS NO VISIBLE SHEEN IN THE HOUSTON SHIP CHANNEL AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT.

properties.content:
Report Details

Incident Time: 2015-10-12 11:38:00
Nearest City: LA
Location:
Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 28.562500, -91.630556 (Explicit)
Report Description
******NESDIS MARINE POLLUTION SURVEILLANCE REPORT***** SEVERAL ANOMALIES ARE SEEN IN THIS IMAGE FROM OCT. 12TH THAT ARE BELIEVED TO BE AREAS OF POSSIBLE OIL. THEY EXTEND APPROXIMATELY 7.6 MILES WEST-NORTHWEST ACROSS GULF WATERS FROM A POTENTIAL POINT SOURCE THAT IS IDENTIFIED AS AN OIL PRODUCTION FACILITY. CLEAR SKIES WERE PRESENT WITH LIGHT WINDS OUT OF THE SOUTH-SOUTHEAST AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE, THOUGH EARLIER SURFACE WINDS HAD INDICATED A GREATER EASTERLY COMPONENT. THIS ALIGNS WELL WITH WESTWARD TRANSPORT OF POSSIBLE OIL SHEENS FROM THE IDENTIFIED POINT SOURCE. IN ADDITION, NRC REPORT #1130646 IDENTIFIED AN UNKNOWN SHEEN ABOUT 20-25 MILES TO THE WEST EARLIER ON 10/12 THAT COULD BE RELATED. UNCERTAINTIES: OTHER FEATURES LIKELY RELATED TO MARINE VEGETATION ARE OBSERVED IN THE IMAGE WHICH DO APPEAR DARK BUT MORE STRINGY THAN THE OBSERVED ANOMALIES. THE ANALYZED AREAS OF POSSIBLE OIL STAND OUT VERY WELL, HAVE SHARP/WELL DEFINED EDGES WITH SHARP TURNS, ARE DARK IN COLOR, AND AT LEAST ONE OF THE AREAS APPEARS TO HAVE SOME HINT OF EMBEDDED SILVER COLOR TO IT WHICH IS ALL CONSISTENT WITH AN OBSERVATION OF AN OIL SHEEN IN MULTI-SPECTAL IMAGERY. POTENTIAL POINT SOURCE IN THE IMAGE UPSTREAM OF THE ANOMALIES ALSO RAISES CONFIDENCE THAT THEY ARE POSSIBLE OIL.
